clue.text: Reserve crew appearing after interval

indicators.note: the crew word is placed after the interval word, following it in the answer

parts.note: in music a twelfth is the interval of an octave plus a fifth
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: A substitute crew turns up once the break is over.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the twelfth man is the substitute fielder kept in reserve; 'crew' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A twelfth man is the cricket team's substitute player, held back as a reserve.

clue.text: Fetching a few following victory

indicators.note: the few-word comes after, following the victory word

parts.note: a victory is a win
a few means some

explanation.surface: A small group goes and gets something after a triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching in the sense of attractive or charming is a synonym of the adjective.

clue.text: Delight in friend climbing, and winning

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the friend word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a side that is winning is up, ahead in the score

explanation.surface: A friend going up a mountain and coming out ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap something up is an idiom for enjoying it eagerly, revelling in it.

clue.text: Agency worker not on time, establishing a pattern

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker placed by an agency
something not on time is late

explanation.surface: An agency temp who always arrives late is setting a bad precedent.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a shape or model to be copied, a pattern for making others.

clue.text: Pretty similar, two small churches famous US men built

indicators.note: the church letters and the famous US men letters are built up into a new arrangement
two says the church abbreviation is taken twice

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Two little chapels put up by celebrated Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built' shuffles CHCH with FAMOUSUSMEN into MUCHOFAMUCHNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'much of a muchness' means things are about the same, with little to choose between them.

clue.text: Chat coming from check-in at terminal

indicators.note: the answer comes out of the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: Talk overheard at the airport check-in desk.
explanation.definitionFit: To natter is to talk idly and at length, a synonym for chatting.

clue.text: Wrong, female supplying superfluous documents

parts.note: bum as an adjective means bad or wrong, as in a bum note

explanation.surface: A woman mistakenly hands over paperwork nobody needs.
explanation.walkthrough: Bumf is British slang for useless paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumf is informal for unwanted or excessive paperwork, the forms and leaflets nobody reads.

clue.text: Big city prohibition on clubs — no ale, bubbly …

parts.note: a bar is a ban or prohibition
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: bubbly says the letters of these words fizz into a new order

explanation.surface: A city bans nightclubs: no beer, only champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bubbly' looks like champagne but shuffles NOALE into ELONA.
explanation.definitionFit: Barcelona is a major Spanish metropolis, the capital of Catalonia.

clue.text: Madeira wine and port unfinished? Yes, knocked over!

indicators.note: unfinished means the port loses its final letter

parts.note: Malmo is a Swedish port city

indicators.note: in a down entry, knocked over means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wine bottle tipped over, a drinker agreeing it was half-empty port.
explanation.walkthrough: MALMO loses its last letter to give MALM; 'knocked over' turns YES into SEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Malmsey is a sweet fortified wine made on the island of Madeira.

clue.text: Unexpected shot

definitions.meaning: a ... decision or election is sudden and unplanned

explanation.surface: A surprise photograph or gunshot.
explanation.definitionFit: Snap means sudden as in a snap election, and is also an informal photograph.

clue.text: Second chapter on king, almost utterly mad fictional character

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second
K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: mad says the remaining letters go wild into a new order
almost means the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A deranged monarch features in a chapter about something that lasts a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims UTTERLY to UTTERL, and 'mad' shuffles it into TURTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mock Turtle is a melancholy creature met by Alice in Lewis Carroll's Wonderland.

clue.text: Make company representative and the Spanish meet

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A firm's rep and a Spaniard get together.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel someone is to force or make them do something.

clue.text: How eggs may be served if done slowly

parts.note: something done is over, finished
to take it easy is to go slowly

explanation.surface: Eggs cooked gently, perhaps at a leisurely breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Over easy describes fried eggs flipped briefly so the yolk stays runny, an American diner style.

clue.text: Close Tate — vandalised after start of violent feud

indicators.note: the close and vandalised pieces come after that opening letter
start of takes only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the close of something is its end

indicators.note: the gallery name is smashed up, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A violent gang wrecks the Tate gallery and forces it to shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vandalised' turns TATE into ETTA. Tate is a London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged, bitter quarrel, often a family blood feud.

clue.text: Type of ticket ordered ready to go off

indicators.note: ordered says the letters of the next word are put in a new order

parts.note: milk that goes off turns sour

explanation.surface: Someone prepared to leave, waiting on a ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' shuffles READY into DAYRE. A day return is a British rail ticket for going and coming back the same day.
explanation.definitionFit: A day return is a kind of railway ticket valid for an outward and return trip in one day.

clue.text: Antelope and steer crossing tracks

indicators.note: crossing means the steer word straddles the tracks word, holding it inside

parts.note: a steer is a castrated bull, an ox
RY is the abbreviation for railway, the tracks

explanation.surface: An antelope and a bullock wander across the railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: The oryx is a large African and Arabian antelope with long straight horns.

clue.text: Serving up endless wine is ominous

indicators.note: in a down entry, serving up means the words are sent upwards, read in reverse
endless means the wine loses its last letter

parts.note: retsina is a Greek resinated wine
taken as written

explanation.surface: A waiter keeps pouring wine without stopping, which bodes ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts RETSINA to RETSIN; 'Serving up' turns RETSINIS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister means threatening or suggesting harm, close to ominous in meaning.

clue.text: Speak about short time in lodge

indicators.note: about means the speaking word goes round the time letter

parts.note: to say is to speak
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Giving a brief talk at a Masonic lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge somewhere is to stay there, living as a guest or lodger.

clue.text: Article on more complex proposition to be proved

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: complex says the letters of the next word are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece setting out a more complicated idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a mathematical statement that must be established by proof.

clue.text: Rebellious at university, confronting elected members

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university
a party elected is in, in office
arms are members, as limbs of the body

explanation.surface: Students facing their newly elected representatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up in arms means protesting angrily, in revolt against something.

clue.text: Bishop in power, a woman's ideal man?

indicators.note: in means the bishop letters sit inside the power word

parts.note: might is power or strength
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A powerful bishop, perhaps every parishioner's dream partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Right is the idiomatic name for the perfect future husband or partner.

clue.text: Stadium beginning to get full

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of the next word

parts.note: round can mean full or plump, as a round face

explanation.surface: A stadium starting to fill up with fans.
explanation.definitionFit: A ground is a sports venue, such as a football or cricket stadium.

clue.text: Look into religious education examination

parts.note: RE is the school subject Religious Education
a search is a close examination

explanation.surface: A test in the school's religion class.
explanation.definitionFit: To research a topic is to investigate or study it closely.

clue.text: Advise some villain for money

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A crook who would pass on secrets for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform someone is to tell or notify them, a close sense of advise.

clue.text: Father describing flightless bird's bone

indicators.note: describing is used in its sense of drawing around, so the father letters encircle the bird

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: A priest giving an account of an ostrich-like bird's skeleton.
explanation.definitionFit: The femur is the thigh bone, the longest in the human body.

clue.text: Crooked force? Untrue, lad discovered

parts.note: F is the physics abbreviation for force

indicators.note: discovered, read as uncovered and laid bare, signals the letters being broken up into a new order

explanation.surface: A police force exposed as dishonest when a young man finds out the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraudulent means dishonest or deceitful, which is what crooked means informally.

clue.text: Huge girl? No end

indicators.note: no end means the name drops its final letter

parts.note: Megan is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Asking whether a very large girl has no limit.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is informal for enormous or very big, as in a mega hit.

clue.text: Sign guides drag off

indicators.note: off means the word drag is taken away from the guides word

parts.note: a dragoman is an interpreter and guide in Arabic- or Turkish-speaking lands
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tour guides wear a sign telling people not to pull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag' looks like a verb, but it is the very letters removed from DRAGOMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent or sign of what is to come.

clue.text: Soldiers recalled pitch covered by leaves

indicators.note: covered by means the turned pitch word sits inside the leaves word

parts.note: deserts as a verb means leaves or abandons

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the pitch word is read backwards

parts.note: tar is pitch, the black sticky substance

explanation.surface: A sports pitch, called back into use, has been buried under fallen leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns TAR into RAT. The Desert Rats were the British 7th Armoured Division in the North African campaign of WWII.
explanation.definitionFit: The Desert Rats is the nickname of a British army division, so its members are soldiers.
